children: REX reported record fiscal second-quarter results for 2026, posting diluted net income per share attributable to common shareholders of $1.06 versus $0.22 in the prior-year quarter. Net income attributable to REX common shareholders was $34.9 million on net sales and revenue of $168.5 million, and gross profit totaled $53.3 million. The quarter included $18.4 million of production tax credit income related to the Section 45Z program and noted regulatory progress on its carbon capture project.
Net sales and revenue: $168.5 million for the three months ended July 31, 2026 (Q2 ’26).
Production tax credit income: $18.4 million included in Q2 ’26 results (net of estimated monetization expenses).
Gross profit: $53.3 million for Q2 ’26, compared with $14.3 million in Q2 ’25.
Net income attributable to REX common shareholders: $34.9 million in Q2 ’26 versus $7.1 million in Q2 ’25.
Basic and diluted net income per share attributable to common shareholders: $1.06 for Q2 ’26 versus $0.22 for Q2 ’25 (based on diluted weighted average shares of 33,090 for Q2 ’26).

Operational footprint: Results reflect interests in six ethanol production facilities; two consolidated facilities (One Earth and NuGen) and four reported as equity in income of unconsolidated affiliates.

Production and sales volumes: Ethanol gallons sold totaled 70.6 million in Q2 ’26 (141.7 million for the six months ended July 31, 2026); distillers corn oil and dried distillers grains sales volumes reported for the period.

One Earth expansion: Construction of the ethanol production expansion at the One Earth facility is on track with testing and commissioning expected following construction completion and full operation anticipated during fiscal 2026.

Carbon capture permitting milestone: Received draft Class VI injection well permits from the U.S. EPA on August 17, 2026, for three injection wells for the One Earth carbon capture and sequestration project; EPA is accepting public comments on the draft permits.
Capital investment: Capital expenditures to date for the One Earth carbon capture and related ethanol expansion at the Gibson City location totaled $191.2 million.
